result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow, poorly maintained sidewalks that are frequently obstructed by utility poles and parked vehicles. There is a lack of formal crossing infrastructure and no physical separation between the walkway and the roadway beyond the parking lane.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles and parked vehicles significantly narrow or block the pedestrian path, potentially forcing people into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street along the sidewalk

hazards.name: Poor Surface Condition
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven sidewalk surfaces create trip hazards for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Visible on both the left and right walkways

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and widen sidewalks to provide a continuous, ADA-compliant path of travel free of obstructions.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections to reduce crossing distances and prevent vehicles from parking too close to corners or blocking walkways.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, well-maintained concrete sidewalk that is significantly interrupted by a large driveway entrance for a surface parking lot. The lack of a buffer between the walkway and the roadway, combined with the potential for vehicle conflicts at the wide curb cut, creates a moderately high-risk environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide driveway curb cut
hazards.description: The expansive entrance increases the distance pedestrians must travel without protection and allows for higher vehicle turning speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground where the sidewalk meets the parking lot entrance

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and fencing near the driveway entrance may obscure the view between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the driveway entrance behind the black fence

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reducing the width of the driveway throat would slow turning traffic and minimize the pedestrian exposure zone.

interventions.title: High-visibility Sidewalk Markings
interventions.description: Applying paint or distinct paving across the driveway would clearly define the pedestrian path and reinforce their right-of-way.

result.summary: The intersection features wide, well-maintained sidewalks and marked zebra crosswalks with curb ramps and tactile paving. While an all-way stop control is present, the environment lacks physical traffic calming measures and contains parked vehicles that may obstruct sightlines at the corners.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners can block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street approaching the intersection.

hazards.name: Lack of Physical Traffic Calming
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway lacks physical measures to slow traffic, relying solely on stop signs which may be ignored.
hazards.location_in_image: The main travel lanes leading into the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility by preventing parking too close to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalks to ensure clear sightlines between all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a wide, paved sidewalk separated from the roadway by a curb and a lane of parallel-parked vehicles. The streetscape is characterized by a large brick building with a mostly blank frontage and a chain-link fence, lacking street trees or other pedestrian-scale amenities.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The large brick wall of the central building provides no visual interest or 'eyes on the street', which can reduce the perceived safety of pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Shade
hazards.description: The absence of street trees or awnings leaves pedestrians fully exposed to the elements, which can be a hazard during extreme heat.

interventions.title: Street Tree Planting
interventions.description: Install street trees along the sidewalk to provide shade, improve air quality, and enhance the aesthetic appeal of the pedestrian environment.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lower-height lighting fixtures specifically for the sidewalk to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians at night.
